title: Glute-Ham Raise
summary: A hamstring exercise on a glute-ham bench that trains knee flexion and hip extension together.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for hamstrings (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.4 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.3 for calves (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly calves total.
Library rating 0.2 for lower back: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Set your feet against the plate with your knees just behind the pad.
Lower your torso forward under control until your body is horizontal.
Pull yourself back up with your hamstrings.

form_cues.cue: Curl back up with the hamstrings
Push your toes into the plate to help start the pull.

mistakes.text: Bending at the hips to make it easier.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
